sky.title: The naked-eye sky (HYG v4.4)
sky.source: HYG database v4.4 (Hipparcos, Yale Bright Star and Gliese catalogues combined), codeberg.org/astronexus/hyg
sky.cuts: V < 6.5 (naked-eye limit), plus named stars to V < 8. Distances from Hipparcos parallaxes (van Leeuwen 2007).
sky.citation: Nash, D. (astronexus) HYG v4.4; ESA 1997 Hipparcos; van Leeuwen 2007, A&A 474, 653
sky.columns_note: ra, dec in degrees (J2000); mag = Johnson V; ci = B-V colour index; dist in parsecs

constellations.title: Constellation lines
constellations.columns_note: pairs of row numbers into sky.csv

milkyway.title: Star counts across the whole sky (Gaia DR3)
milkyway.query: SELECT GAIA_HEALPIX_INDEX(6, source_id), COUNT(*) FROM gaiadr3.gaia_source WHERE random_index < 36000000 GROUP BY 1
milkyway.cuts: A 2% random subsample of the 1.8 billion Gaia sources, counted in 49,152 HEALPix cells, resampled to a 720 x 360 RA/Dec grid; log scale.
milkyway.citation: Gaia Collaboration, Vallenari et al. 2023, A&A 674, A1 (Gaia DR3)

nearby.title: Stars within 100 parsecs (Gaia DR3 / Gaia Catalogue of Nearby Stars)
nearby.source: Gaia archive, external.gaiaedr3_gcns_main_1 (Gaia Collaboration, Smart et al. 2021, A&A 649, A6), plus gaiadr3.astrophysical_parameters
nearby.query: parallax > 10 mas, then the HR-diagram quality cuts of Gaia Collaboration, Babusiaux et al. 2018: parallax/error > 10, G flux S/N > 50, BP and RP S/N > 20, BP/RP excess factor between 1.0+0.015(BP-RP)^2 and 1.3+0.06(BP-RP)^2, RUWE < 1.4.
nearby.cuts: 207176 stars pass. Shipped: every red giant (M_G < 3, BP-RP > 0.9; 683), 4000 of 12779 white dwarfs (GCNS probability > 0.5) and 32000 of the other stars, chosen at random. Gaia temperatures, radii, masses and luminosities attached where Gaia has them (a random 6000 were looked up).
nearby.citation: Gaia Collaboration, Vallenari et al. 2023, A&A 674, A1 (Gaia DR3); Gaia Collaboration, Smart et al. 2021, A&A 649, A6
nearby.columns_note: parallax in mas; G magnitude; BP-RP colour; proper motions in mas/yr; rv km/s; teff K; radius, mass, lum in solar units (Gaia FLAME)

clusters.title: Star clusters (Gaia DR3)
clusters.query: Cone around each cluster centre with loose parallax and proper-motion windows (see fetch_gaia.py). The Pleiades file is the whole 3-degree field with parallax > 2 mas, so members must be picked out by the player.
clusters.literature: E(B-V), ages and distances, used only to check answers: Gaia Collaboration, Babusiaux et al. 2018 (A&A 616, A10); Baumgardt & Vasiliev 2021 (MNRAS 505, 5957) for NGC 6397.
clusters.citation: Gaia Collaboration, Vallenari et al. 2023, A&A 674, A1 (Gaia DR3)

binaries.title: Double-lined spectroscopic binaries that also eclipse (Gaia DR3)
binaries.source: Gaia archive: gaiadr3.nss_two_body_orbit (nss_solution_type = SB2) matched to gaiadr3.vari_eclipsing_binary
binaries.cuts: Kept when the eclipse period agrees with the orbit period to 0.2% and both velocity amplitudes exceed 20 km/s. Eclipses mean the orbit is seen nearly edge-on, so sin i is close to 1.
binaries.citation: Gaia Collaboration, Vallenari et al. 2023, A&A 674, A1 (Gaia DR3); Gaia Collaboration, Arenou et al. 2023, A&A 674, A34; Mowlavi et al. 2023, A&A 674, A16
binaries.columns_note: period days; K1, K2, gamma km/s; w degrees; T0 = time of periastron (days, Gaia reference epoch 2016.0); depth = primary eclipse depth (mag)

torres.title: Accurate stellar masses (Torres, Andersen & Gimenez 2010)
torres.license: Published data; used for teaching with citation
torres.columns_note: mass, radius, logL in solar units; teff K; period days

cepheids_ogle.title: Classical Cepheids in the Magellanic Clouds (OGLE-IV)
cepheids_ogle.source: OGLE Collection of Variable Stars, www.astrouw.edu.pl/ogle/ogle4/OCVS/{smc,lmc}/cep/cepF.dat and ident.dat
cepheids_ogle.cuts: Fundamental-mode classical Cepheids with a mean I magnitude.
cepheids_ogle.citation: Soszynski et al. 2015, Acta Astron. 65, 297 (OGLE-IV Cepheids)
cepheids_ogle.license: OGLE data, free to use with citation
cepheids_ogle.columns_note: P days; I, V intensity-mean magnitudes; Iamp = I-band amplitude

cepheids_gaia.title: Classical Cepheids measured by Gaia (DR3)
cepheids_gaia.source: Gaia archive: gaiadr3.vari_cepheid joined to gaiadr3.gaia_source
cepheids_gaia.cuts: type_best_classification = 'DCEP', fundamental mode. Milky Way Cepheids kept only with parallax/error > 5 and RUWE < 1.4.
cepheids_gaia.citation: Gaia Collaboration, Vallenari et al. 2023, A&A 674, A1 (Gaia DR3); Ripepi et al. 2023, A&A 674, A17
cepheids_gaia.columns_note: parallax mas (no zero-point correction applied here; the app adds +0.017 mas, Lindegren et al. 2021); P days; G, BP, RP intensity-averaged magnitudes

cepheid_lc.title: Cepheid light curves (OGLE-IV, I band)
cepheid_lc.license: OGLE data, free to use with citation

pulsars.title: Pulsars (ATNF Pulsar Catalogue)
pulsars.license: ATNF Pulsar Catalogue, free to use with citation
pulsars.columns_note: P seconds; Pdot s/s (blank when unmeasured); binary 1 = in a binary; type: AXP, HE, NRAD, RRAT etc.; dist kpc from dispersion measure; ra, dec J2000 degrees; dm pc/cm^3

exoplanets.title: Confirmed exoplanets (NASA Exoplanet Archive)
exoplanets.source: exoplanetarchive.ipac.caltech.edu TAP, table pscomppars (one row per planet)
exoplanets.citation: NASA Exoplanet Archive, operated by Caltech under contract with NASA (DOI 10.26133/NEA13)
exoplanets.columns_note: orbital period days; semi-major axis AU; mass and radius in Jupiter units; eqt K; star teff K, mass and radius solar; distance pc; massprov: measured, minimum (M sin i) or estimated from radius (Chen & Kipping 2017)

kepler.title: Two transiting planets seen by Kepler (quarter 2): HAT-P-7 b and HAT-P-11 b
kepler.cuts: PDCSAP flux, finite values, divided by a 2-day running median; points more than 5 sigma above the median removed.
kepler.citation: Borucki et al. 2010, Science 327, 977 (Kepler); Pal et al. 2008, ApJ 680, 1450 (HAT-P-7 b); Bakos et al. 2010, ApJ 710, 1724 (HAT-P-11 b)
kepler.columns_note: t = BJD - 2454833 (Kepler time, days); f = relative flux

microlensing.title: Microlensing light curves (OGLE-IV Early Warning System, 2019)
microlensing.cuts: Points within 200 days of the peak.
microlensing.citation: Udalski 2003, Acta Astron. 53, 291 (EWS); Udalski, Szymanski & Szymanski 2015, Acta Astron. 65, 1 (OGLE-IV)
microlensing.license: OGLE asks to be contacted before its EWS photometry is used in publications. Fine for private study; ask OGLE before sharing this page publicly.

smallbodies.title: Asteroids and trans-Neptunian objects (JPL Small-Body Database)
smallbodies.cuts: Numbered asteroids brighter than H = 15.5 (121409): a random 30% of the main belt (inner, middle and outer alike) plus every other class; every TNO (8397). a < 120 AU, bound orbits.
smallbodies.citation: JPL Solar System Dynamics, Small-Body Database
smallbodies.columns_note: a AU; e; i degrees; H absolute magnitude

globulars.title: Globular clusters of the Milky Way (Harris catalogue, 2010 edition)
globulars.columns_note: l, b Galactic degrees; distances kpc; X toward the Galactic centre, Y in the direction of rotation, Z to the north Galactic pole (Sun-centred, kpc)

rotation_curves.title: Rotation curves of 175 disk galaxies (SPARC)
rotation_curves.columns_note: R kpc; Vobs, eV observed speed and error km/s; Vgas, Vdisk, Vbul: speeds the gas, the stellar disk (for M/L = 1 at 3.6 um) and the bulge would give on their own, km/s

sparc.title: SPARC galaxy table
sparc.columns_note: T Hubble type code (0 = S0 ... 11 = BCD); D Mpc; L36 = 3.6 um luminosity, 1e9 Lsun; Reff kpc; MHI 1e9 Msun; Vflat km/s (0 = no flat part); Q quality 1-3

galaxies.title: Nearby galaxies with Galaxy Zoo classifications (SDSS DR18)
galaxies.source: skyserver.sdss.org/dr18, SpecObj x PhotoObj x zooSpec
galaxies.query: class = 'GALAXY', zWarning = 0, 0.02 < z < 0.05, a quarter of objects (objID mod 4 = 0)
galaxies.cuts: Petrosian magnitudes corrected for Galactic extinction; r < 17.77 (the spectroscopic survey limit); 14000 kept at random. Velocity dispersions kept when error < 20%.
galaxies.citation: SDSS DR18 (Almeida et al. 2023, ApJS 267, 44); Galaxy Zoo: Lintott et al. 2011, MNRAS 410, 166
galaxies.columns_note: u, g, r magnitudes; r50 = half-light radius arcsec; sigma = stellar velocity dispersion km/s; p_el, p_sp = Galaxy Zoo vote fractions (debiased) for elliptical and spiral

coma.title: Galaxies toward the Coma cluster (SDSS DR18)
coma.columns_note: z redshift; r, g extinction-corrected magnitudes

_about.note: Every number in the Observatorium comes from these files. See pipeline/README.md to rebuild them.

photographs.title: Photographs of the sky (photo layer)
photographs.source: All-sky: ESO/S. Brunier, the Milky Way panorama (eso0932a), CC BY 4.0. Close-ups (The Pleiades (M45), Praesepe (M44), M67, NGC 6397, 61 Cygni, The Orion Nebula (M42), Betelgeuse, Rigel, Gaia DR3 3684484600212307712, The Small Magellanic Cloud, The Crab Nebula (M1), HAT-P-7, Toward the Galactic bulge: OGLE-2019-BLG-0148, 47 Tucanae, M13, The Andromeda galaxy (M31), NGC 3198, The Coma cluster, M87, a giant elliptical, M101, a spiral, M51, the Whirlpool, The Cosmic Horseshoe (an Einstein ring), The Einstein Cross (Q2237+0305), Abell 370, Abell 1689, MACS J0416.1-2403): DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys DR9 (legacysurvey.org); Digitized Sky Survey 2 (STScI/NASA; POSS-II Caltech/Palomar, UK Schmidt AAO), via NASA SkyView; Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS DR18 image cutout service).
photographs.cuts: DSS2 red and blue plates stretched and combined into colour (green = their mean); first-epoch DSS plates fill fields with no DSS2 plate in one colour. Each close-up is a gnomonic projection, north up, east left.
photographs.license: ESO panorama CC BY 4.0. DSS: free for research and education with acknowledgement. SDSS and Legacy Surveys images: public, with acknowledgement.
photographs.citation: Brunier (ESO) 2009, eso0932a; Lasker et al. 1990 / Reid et al. 1991 (DSS); SDSS DR18; Dey et al. 2019 (Legacy Surveys)

sunspots.title: Sunspot number since 1700
sunspots.citation: SILSO World Data Center, Royal Observatory of Belgium, Brussels: International Sunspot Number, version 2.0
sunspots.columns_note: year (mid-year); sn = yearly mean total sunspot number

grbs.title: Gamma-ray bursts (Fermi GBM)
grbs.cuts: T90 > 0; positions from the GBM catalogue (typical error a few degrees)

spectra.title: Stellar spectra across the spectral sequence
spectra.source: SDSS DR17 spec-lite files (data.sdss.org), brightest-S/N star of each subclass B6, A0, F5, G2, K3, M2
spectra.cuts: Flux binned to 2 nm (median), divided by its 99th percentile.

supernovae.title: Type Ia supernovae (Pantheon+)
supernovae.cuts: z_HD > 0.01, Cepheid calibrators removed, repeat observations of one supernova averaged (inverse-variance)
supernovae.citation: Scolnic et al. 2022, ApJ 938, 113; Brout et al. 2022, ApJ 938, 110

cmb_spectrum.title: The CMB spectrum (COBE FIRAS)
cmb_spectrum.cuts: Monopole spectrum with 1-sigma uncertainties (converted from kJy/sr to MJy/sr)

cmb_power.title: The CMB temperature power spectrum (Planck 2018)
cmb_power.cuts: l < 30 unbinned; l >= 30 in bins of 30; error = mean of the lower and upper 1-sigma
cmb_power.citation: Planck Collaboration 2020, A&A 641, A5 and A6
cmb_power.license: ESA Planck Legacy Archive, free use with acknowledgement

zspec.title: SDSS spectra for measuring redshifts
zspec.cuts: Highest S/N spectrum of each kind with no masked pixels; median-binned to 0.4 nm; scaled to the 99.5th percentile

bpt.title: Emission lines and properties of SDSS galaxies (MPA-JHU)
bpt.cuts: 0.02 < z < 0.2, every fifth fibre, H-alpha, H-beta, [OIII] 5007 and [NII] 6584 all detected at 3 sigma, log M > 7; a random 20,000 of them
bpt.citation: Brinchmann et al. 2004; Kauffmann et al. 2003; Tremonti et al. 2004

frbs.title: Fast radio bursts
frbs.cuts: All bursts in the table; z only for localized hosts
frbs.citation: Prochaska & Zheng 2019; Macquart et al. 2020; Heintz et al. 2020; Gordon et al. 2023 (as compiled in the FRBs repository)

gw.title: Gravitational-wave mergers (GWTC)
gw.cuts: Events with source-frame masses and p_astro >= 0.5; medians of the posteriors
gw.citation: LIGO Scientific, Virgo and KAGRA Collaborations, GWTC-1 to GWTC-5 (GWOSC)

photfield.title: An r-band image for photometry
photfield.source: legacysurvey.org fits-cutout (ls-dr9, r, 0.262"/pixel, 200 x 200); SDSS Star table
photfield.cuts: Pixel values in nanomaggies (AB zero point 22.5), multiplied by 1000 and rounded
photfield.citation: Dey et al. 2019 (Legacy Surveys); SDSS DR18

skybands.title: The whole sky at other wavelengths
skybands.source: NASA SkyView all-sky Car projections, Galactic, 0.25 deg/pixel
skybands.cuts: Log stretch (radio, HI, IR, H-alpha), smoothed log stretch (X-ray and gamma counts), symmetric linear stretch (CMB)
skybands.citation: Haslam et al. 1982 (408 MHz all-sky survey), via NASA SkyView; HI4PI Collaboration 2016, via NASA SkyView; NASA/WMAP Science Team (9-year ILC map), via NASA SkyView; IRIS (Miville-Deschenes & Lagache 2005, reprocessed IRAS), via NASA SkyView; Finkbeiner 2003 (H-alpha composite), via NASA SkyView; ROSAT All-Sky Survey diffuse background, R6 band (Snowden et al. 1997), via NASA SkyView; CGRO/EGRET (NASA), via NASA SkyView
skybands.license: NASA SkyView; each survey with acknowledgement

rv51peg.title: Radial velocities of 51 Pegasi (Lick)
rv51peg.cuts: All Lick velocities of HD 217014; JD − 2400000

s2.title: The star S2 around Sgr A*
s2.cuts: Epochs with a position or a velocity of S2

ellipticals.title: SDSS ellipticals with velocity dispersions
ellipticals.cuts: 0.02 < z < 0.08, Galaxy Zoo p_el (debiased) > 0.8, 60 < σ < 420 km/s with error < 15, r < 17.7 (extinction corrected); first 8,000
ellipticals.citation: Abdurro'uf et al. 2022 (SDSS); Lintott et al. 2011 (Galaxy Zoo)

ogle_events.title: OGLE-IV EWS microlensing events, 2019
ogle_events.cuts: Events with 0.3 < t_E < 600 d and u0 > 0 from OGLE's single-lens fits
ogle_events.citation: Udalski et al. 2015, Acta Astron. 65, 1 (OGLE-IV); OGLE EWS
ogle_events.license: OGLE: ask before use in publications

orbits.title: Full orbits of bright asteroids and TNOs
orbits.cuts: Numbered objects with H < 13, a < 120 AU, bound; mean anomaly moved to JD 2461041.5 (2026 Jan 1)
orbits.citation: JPL Solar System Dynamics, Small-Body Database
